workloads.sieve-array:
def benchmark
  flags = Array.new(256, 1)
  p = 2
  while p * p < 256
    if flags[p] != 0
      k = p * p
      while k < 256
        flags[k] = 0
        k += p
      end
    end
    p += 1
  end
  total = 0
  i = 2
  while i < 256
    total += flags[i]
    i += 1
  end
  total
end
workloads.towers-recursive:
def towers(n)
  n == 0 ? 0 : 1 + towers(n - 1) + towers(n - 1)
end

def benchmark
  towers(18)
end
workloads.queens-backtracking:
def benchmark
  cols = Array.new(8, 0)
  safe = lambda do |row, col|
    prior = 0
    while prior < row
      placed = cols[prior]
      return false if placed == col || (placed - col).abs == row - prior
      prior += 1
    end
    true
  end
  place = nil
  place = lambda do |row|
    return 1 if row == 8
    total = 0
    col = 0
    while col < 8
      if safe.call(row, col)
        cols[row] = col
        total += place.call(row + 1)
      end
      col += 1
    end
    total
  end
  place.call(0)
end
workloads.heap-permute:
def benchmark
  values = (0...8).to_a
  permute = nil
  permute = lambda do |n|
    return 1 if n == 1
    total = 0
    i = 0
    while i < n
      total += permute.call(n - 1)
      j = n.even? ? i : 0
      values[j], values[n - 1] = values[n - 1], values[j]
      i += 1
    end
    total
  end
  permute.call(8)
end
workloads.ackermann-deep:
def ack(m, n)
  return n + 1 if m == 0
  return ack(m - 1, 1) if n == 0
  ack(m - 1, ack(m, n - 1))
end

def benchmark
  ack(3, 8)
end
workloads.tak-branching:
def tak(x, y, z)
  x <= y ? z : tak(tak(x - 1, y, z), tak(y - 1, z, x), tak(z - 1, x, y))
end

def benchmark
  tak(18, 12, 6)
end
workloads.collatz-range:
def benchmark
  total = 0
  n = 1
  while n <= 10_000
    value = n
    while value != 1
      value = value.even? ? value / 2 : 3 * value + 1
      total += 1
    end
    n += 1
  end
  total
end
workloads.matrix-multiply:
def benchmark
  a = (1..16).to_a
  b = [1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 0, 3, 6, 9, 12]
  c = Array.new(16, 0)
  iteration = 0
  while iteration < 100
    row = 0
    while row < 4
      col = 0
      while col < 4
        value = 0
        k = 0
        while k < 4
          value += a[row * 4 + k] * b[k * 4 + col]
          k += 1
        end
        c[row * 4 + col] = value
        col += 1
      end
      row += 1
    end
    iteration += 1
  end
  c.sum
end
